review_question: WP603 must make the recursion-depth origin unambiguous. F2-WP-601 exposes ChildResourceBudget.max_nested_depth as a non-negative integer but does not itself define whether the first delegated child consumes depth 1 or whether max_nested_depth counts only descendants spawned by that child. The WP603 claim names R0 as no child recursion and R1/R2/R3 as recursion depth 1/2/3. Without an explicit mapping, a formally deterministic router can still admit an off-by-one recursion budget or unnecessarily require a NativeChildRequest on DIRECT_SMALL/R0.
counterhypotheses: R0 means a delegated child may run but may not spawn descendants; then DELEGATE_BUILD+R0 is valid and max_nested_depth=0 is sufficient.
R0 means no child exists at all; then DELEGATE_BUILD+R0 is contradictory and the first delegated child is R1.
DIRECT_SMALL+R0 should not require any NativeChildRequest identity because no child boundary is consumed; requiring one would couple the direct path to an irrelevant downstream authority.
required_discriminator: Define in the WP603 source contract exactly what depth zero is relative to the root task and delegated child.
Test DELEGATE_BUILD with selected R0 and ChildResourceBudget.max_nested_depth=0 against the chosen definition.
Test the R1/R2/R3 boundary at exactly-equal budget and one-below budget to expose off-by-one admission.

Test DIRECT_SMALL+R0 without a NativeChildRequest if the design intends the direct path to remain independent of child identity; otherwise document and test why a child request is required even though no delegation occurs.
Keep DIRECT_SMALL+R1/R2/R3 fail-closed as already required by the active claim.
recommended_resolution: The active WP603 mutation owner should absorb this as explicit source-level terminology plus boundary tests before acceptance. If the implementation already chooses one semantic mapping, preserve that choice in canonical constants/docstrings and tests so later WP604 nested-spawn handling cannot reinterpret depth differently.
next_exact_action: When recursion_router.py lands on the active WP603 branch, review the exact R0/R1/R2/R3-to-max_nested_depth mapping and convert this review gate into an executable counterexample only if the source leaves an off-by-one or irrelevant-dependency path open.
